{
  "study_id": "SBT-002",
  "analysis_claims": [],
  "findings": [
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F1",
      "proposition": "Prioritise Flex for broad-audience development within the eligible study audience, while retaining Plus. Flex has higher weighted top-two appeal: 61.0% versus 54.0% (+7.0 percentage points; Holm p=0.0112), exceeding the 5-point commercial threshold. Purchase intent is 53.2% versus 50.4% (+2.8 points; Holm p=0.311), providing no demonstrated advantage.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "concept_metrics.appeal_5.Flex",
        "concept_metrics.appeal_5.Plus",
        "pairwise.appeal_5[0]",
        "concept_metrics.purchase_intent_5.Flex",
        "concept_metrics.purchase_intent_5.Plus",
        "pairwise.purchase_intent_5[0]"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Development recommendation supported by statistically significant appeal superiority and a commercially material point estimate; purchase-intent superiority is unproven.",
      "qualification": "Each concept has n=700; effective bases are Flex 650.1 and Plus 645.6. Nonsignificance does not establish equivalence. Purchase intent assumes a reasonable price and measures stated likelihood to subscribe or try, not observed demand. Commercial materiality describes the estimated difference, not proof that the population difference exceeds 5 points.",
      "topic_cluster": "advancement"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F2",
      "proposition": "Retain Plus for targeted development and testing among food explorers. Explorer appeal is 72.1% for Plus versus 60.1% for Flex, and purchase intent is 63.9% versus 52.4%. Among non-explorers, the numerical pattern reverses: appeal is 48.4% versus 61.2%, and purchase intent is 46.2% versus 53.5%. The pre-specified differences between the groups' Plus-minus-Flex gaps are 24.85 points for appeal (Holm p=0.0000137) and 18.81 points for purchase intent (Holm p=0.000968).",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "strategic_subgroup.food_explorer.appeal_5",
        "strategic_subgroup.food_explorer.purchase_intent_5",
        "strategic_subgroup.non_explorer.appeal_5",
        "strategic_subgroup.non_explorer.purchase_intent_5",
        "interactions.appeal_5",
        "interactions.purchase_intent_5"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Confirmatory interaction evidence supports different relative performance by audience and a targeted development recommendation.",
      "qualification": "Explorer bases: Plus n=234, effective n=223.5; Flex n=236, effective n=225.4. Non-explorer bases: Plus n=466, effective n=449.1; Flex n=464, effective n=446.3. Interaction tests do not establish adjusted superiority within either subgroup. Explorer status was defined before exposure as mean agreement across P1–P3 >=4, including willingness to pay more for distinctive food.",
      "topic_cluster": "target_audience"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F6",
      "proposition": "Deprioritise Simple in its tested form. Its appeal is 41.1%, below Flex by 19.9 points and Plus by 12.9; purchase intent is 40.4%, below Flex by 12.8 and Plus by 10.0. All four estimated differences exceed the 5-point commercial threshold and have Holm p<0.001. Simple nevertheless records 92.9% top-two ease of understanding and 57.3% credibility.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "concept_metrics.appeal_5.Simple",
        "concept_metrics.purchase_intent_5.Simple",
        "pairwise.appeal_5[1]",
        "pairwise.appeal_5[2]",
        "pairwise.purchase_intent_5[1]",
        "pairwise.purchase_intent_5[2]",
        "concept_metrics.understanding_5.Simple",
        "concept_metrics.credibility_5.Simple"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Significant disadvantages on both primary outcomes, with commercially material point estimates, support deprioritisation.",
      "qualification": "Each concept has n=700; Simple effective n=645.2. The recommendation concerns this stimulus, not all propositions based on simplicity. Understanding and credibility scores do not establish causal effects on appeal or intent.",
      "topic_cluster": "portfolio_priority"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F3",
      "proposition": "Test clearer communication and a more believable, relevant proposition for Plus. Flex exceeds Plus on ease of understanding (95.7% versus 32.3%; +63.5 points), credibility (62.3% versus 42.2%; +20.1), and relevance (63.7% versus 49.4%; +14.3); all Holm p<0.000001. Expected value for money shows no demonstrated difference: 56.3% for Flex versus 56.7% for Plus (Holm p=0.900).",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "concept_metrics.understanding_5",
        "pairwise.understanding_5[0]",
        "concept_metrics.credibility_5",
        "pairwise.credibility_5[0]",
        "concept_metrics.relevance_5",
        "pairwise.relevance_5[0]",
        "concept_metrics.value_5",
        "pairwise.value_5[0]"
      ],
      "importance": "secondary",
      "claim_strength": "Significant diagnostic differences with commercially material point estimates; proposed improvements remain hypotheses.",
      "qualification": "All percentages are weighted top-two scores; n=700 per concept. These comparisons do not show that changing understanding, credibility or relevance would improve primary outcomes. Value for money assumes a modest premium and does not measure willingness to pay a specific price; nonsignificance does not establish equivalence.",
      "topic_cluster": "development_priorities"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F4",
      "proposition": "Preserve Plus's distinctiveness while addressing its mixed reception. Uniqueness is 81.4%, versus 47.9% for Flex and 34.3% for Simple: advantages of 33.5 and 47.1 points, both Holm p<0.000001. Plus also has more maximum appeal ratings than Flex (31.3% versus 26.7%) and more bottom-two ratings (23.8% versus 16.4%), despite lower top-two appeal.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "concept_metrics.uniqueness_5",
        "pairwise.uniqueness_5[0]",
        "pairwise.uniqueness_5[2]",
        "concept_metrics.appeal_5.Plus.distribution_pct",
        "concept_metrics.appeal_5.Flex.distribution_pct",
        "concept_metrics.appeal_5.Plus.bottom2_pct",
        "concept_metrics.appeal_5.Flex.bottom2_pct"
      ],
      "importance": "secondary",
      "claim_strength": "Confirmed uniqueness advantages; descriptive evidence of a more divided appeal distribution.",
      "qualification": "Each concept has n=700. Maximum-rating and bottom-two differences have no supplied adjusted tests. Distinctiveness alone neither establishes demand nor explains the audience interaction.",
      "topic_cluster": "distinctiveness"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F5",
      "proposition": "Use Plus's premium-conviction result only as conditional evidence. Among routed respondents, weighted top-two premium conviction is 78.8% for Plus, 50.1% for Flex and 37.7% for Simple. Plus's conditional advantages are 28.7 points over Flex (Holm p=5.08e-25) and 41.1 over Simple (Holm p=5.14e-51). However, only 69.0% of Plus's assigned respondents qualified, compared with 99.1% for Flex and 99.7% for Simple.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "concept_metrics.premium_value_5",
        "pairwise.premium_value_5[0]",
        "pairwise.premium_value_5[2]",
        "routing.premium_value_5"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Significant comparisons among differently selected routed populations; no unconditional premium-superiority claim.",
      "qualification": "Eligibility requires understanding_5 >=3, including the midpoint. Eligible bases: Plus n=483, effective n=444.4; Flex n=694, effective n=644.6; Simple n=698, effective n=643.4. Routing percentages are unweighted; outcome percentages use wt_final. Post-exposure selection differs sharply across concepts, so randomisation does not ensure comparable routed populations. Excluded responses are neither failures nor zeros. Premium conviction is not willingness to pay.",
      "topic_cluster": "premium_evidence"
    }
  ],
  "story": {
    "beats": [
      {
        "order": 1,
        "finding_refs": ["F1", "F6"],
        "headline_intent": "Prioritise Flex for broad development and deprioritise Simple in its current form.",
        "analytical_relationship": "Primary outcomes support the portfolio recommendation while leaving Flex-versus-Plus purchase-intent superiority unresolved."
      },
      {
        "order": 2,
        "finding_refs": ["F2"],
        "headline_intent": "Give Plus a targeted development path among food explorers.",
        "analytical_relationship": "Pre-specified interaction evidence qualifies the total-audience recommendation without establishing within-subgroup superiority."
      },
      {
        "order": 3,
        "finding_refs": ["F4", "F3"],
        "headline_intent": "Preserve Plus's distinctiveness and test improvements to clarity, credibility and relevance.",
        "analytical_relationship": "Diagnostic comparisons and the appeal distribution identify development hypotheses, not causal drivers."
      },
      {
        "order": 4,
        "finding_refs": ["F5"],
        "headline_intent": "Keep premium conviction conditional on who answered.",
        "analytical_relationship": "Unequal post-exposure routing limits how premium evidence can support advancement."
      }
    ]
  },
  "method_notes": [
    "Independently checked the prior draft against the four supplied study files. No tools, external sources or raw data were used. analysis_claims is empty because all findings use supplied analysis tables. Evidence references are exact paths within analysis_results.json; array indices are zero-based.",
    "No numerical or base errors were identified in the retained prior-draft claims. Corrected 'value for money does not distinguish them' to 'no demonstrated difference' to avoid implying equivalence. Clarified that commercial materiality concerns point estimates, not a statistical test against a 5-point margin.",
    "Restricted the broad-audience recommendation explicitly to the eligible study audience, clarified purchase intent as likelihood to subscribe or try, and expanded the explorer definition to acknowledge its willingness-to-pay component. Reclassified diagnostic development priorities as secondary and removed causal-sounding language about Simple's strengths translating into outcomes.",
    "This synthetic randomised monadic study has 2,100 UK adults aged 18–64 with meal-kit openness >=3, including 'might or might not'; n=700 per concept. Findings support fictional development decisions only, not market or customer validation.",
    "Outcome percentages use wt_final and valid question bases. Top-two means ratings 4–5; bottom-two means 1–2. Ordinal distributions were retained for interpretation; means were not used to rank concepts. Blank/not-asked responses are excluded, not scored zero.",
    "Full-cell weighted totals are Flex 703.52, Plus 696.32 and Simple 700.16; Kish effective bases are 650.13, 645.63 and 645.23. Weighted totals and effective bases are not respondent counts.",
    "Supplied inference uses Kish effective-sample-size Wald comparisons of independent cells, with Holm adjustment across three concept pairs within each metric and alpha=0.05. Adjustment is not across every metric reported. The two pre-specified Plus-minus-Flex interactions form a separate Holm-adjusted family.",
    "Food explorer is the only confirmatory strategic subgroup. Its interaction tests establish heterogeneity, not adjusted within-subgroup superiority. Exploratory demographic cuts were not used for headline recommendations.",
    "Figures are rounded from unrounded tables, so displayed percentages may not subtract exactly to displayed differences. Statistical significance, the 5-percentage-point commercial threshold, and development judgment are separate. Advancement means further development and testing, not launch approval."
  ]
}
